```{r module-trajectory-pathway-figure, fig.width=22, fig.height=14, fig.keep='all', results='asis'}
    scale_fill_manual(values = celltype_colors) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of genes", title = "Gene composition") +
    theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
    )
}

# --- Panel C: trajectory per cell type (Corregido: colores consistentes) -----
compute_celltype_module_eigengene <- function(mod, ct, min_features = 3) {
  feats <- gene_celltype_module %>%
    filter(module == mod, celltype == ct) %>%
    pull(gene_celltype)
  
  if (length(feats) < min_features) return(NULL)
  
  sub_mat <- pseudobulk_hvg[feats, , drop = FALSE]
  
  me <- tryCatch(
    moduleEigengenes(t(sub_mat), colors = rep("ct", length(feats)))$eigengenes,
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(me)) return(NULL)
  
  mice <- colnames(sub_mat)
  data.frame(
    sample_id = mice,
    celltype  = ct,
    ME        = me[[1]],
    age       = age_num_lookup[mice],
    n_genes   = length(feats)
  )
}

plot_module_trend_by_celltype <- function(mod) {
  cts <- unique(gene_celltype_module$celltype[gene_celltype_module$module == mod])
  
  df_all <- bind_rows(lapply(cts, function(ct) compute_celltype_module_eigengene(mod, ct)))
  if (is.null(df_all) || nrow(df_all) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  row <- module_trajectory %>% filter(module == mod)
  subtitle_txt <- if (nrow(row) == 1) {
    paste0("Pooled module: ", tolower(row$shape), " / ", row$category,
           ", p-value = ", signif(row$p_value, 3))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  
  ggplot(df_all, aes(x = age, y = ME, color = celltype, fill = celltype)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 1.3, se = TRUE, alpha = 0.12, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = celltype_colors, name = "Cell type") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = celltype_colors, name = "Cell type") +
    labs(x = "Age", y = "Cell-type-restricted eigengene",
         title = paste0("Module ", mod, " -- trajectory by cell type"),
         subtitle = subtitle_txt) +
    theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "grey40")
    )
}

# --- Helper: placeholder panel cuando un modulo/base de datos no tiene
# terminos de enriquecimiento -- asi GO_BP y Reactome siempre ocupan su
# columna en la figura combinada, en vez de desaparecer cuando no hay datos --
empty_pathway_panel <- function(title_txt) {
  ggplot() +
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0,
             label = "No enrichment terms\nfor this module/database",
             size = 3.5, color = "grey55", fontface = "italic") +
    xlim(-1, 1) + ylim(-1, 1) +
    labs(title = title_txt) +
    theme_void(base_size = 10) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold", hjust = 0))
}

# --- Panel D: pathway bubble matrix split by cell type -----------------------
plot_module_pathway_bubble <- function(mod, database_label, n_top_per_ct = 5, n_terms_max = 12) {
  df_db <- enrichment_by_module_celltype %>%
    filter(module == mod, database == database_label)
  if (nrow(df_db) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  top_terms_per_ct <- df_db %>%
    group_by(celltype) %>%
    arrange(p.adjust) %>%
    slice_head(n = n_top_per_ct) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pull(Description) %>%
    unique()
  
  if (length(top_terms_per_ct) > n_terms_max) {
    top_terms_per_ct <- df_db %>%
      group_by(Description) %>%
      summarise(best_p = min(p.adjust), .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(best_p) %>%
      slice_head(n = n_terms_max) %>%
      pull(Description)
  }
  
  n_genes_mod <- gene_counts_by_module_celltype %>%
    filter(module == mod) %>%
    dplyr::select(celltype, n_genes)
  
  df_plot <- df_db %>%
    filter(Description %in% top_terms_per_ct) %>%
    left_join(n_genes_mod, by = "celltype") %>%
    mutate(pct_genes = 100 * Count / n_genes,
           neg_log_fdr = -log10(p.adjust)) %>%
    order_go_terms(desc_col = "Description", p_col = "p.adjust")
  
  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = celltype, y = Description)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = pct_genes, fill = activity_score),
               pch = 21, color = "grey20", stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#4575b4", mid = "white", high = "#d73027",
                         midpoint = 0, name = "Activity\nscore (Z)") +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "% genes", range = c(2, 7)) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(40)) +
    labs(x = "Cell type", y = NULL, title = paste0(database_label, " - Enriched Terms"),
         subtitle = "Size = % of module genes annotated to term (not filtered by significance)") +
    theme_pub(base_size = 9.5) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8.5),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, lineheight = 0.85),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey92"),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.box = "vertical",
          legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.5, color = "grey40"))
}

# --- Panel E: canonical-pathway lollipop (-log10 FDR) -----------------------
plot_module_pathway_lollipop <- function(mod, database_label, n_terms = 10) {
  df_db <- enrichment_by_module_celltype %>%
    filter(module == mod, database == database_label)
  if (nrow(df_db) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  df_top <- df_db %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Description) %>%
    dplyr::slice_min(p.adjust, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p.adjust) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = n_terms) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(neg_log_fdr = -log10(p.adjust),
                  Description = factor(Description, levels = rev(Description)))
  
  ggplot(df_top, aes(x = neg_log_fdr, y = Description)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = neg_log_fdr, y = Description, yend = Description),
                 color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = celltype), pch = 21, color = "grey20", size = 3.5, stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = celltype_colors, name = "Best cell type", drop = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(40)) +
    labs(x = "-log10(FDR)", y = NULL, title = paste0(database_label, " - Top Significance"),
         subtitle = "Color = cell type with lowest FDR") +
    theme_pub(base_size = 9.5) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, lineheight = 0.85),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.5, color = "grey40"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"))
}

# --- Standalone Heatmap por Base de Datos -----------------------------------
create_module_pathway_heatmap <- function(mod, database_label, n_top = 8) {
  df_db <- enrichment_by_module_celltype %>%
    filter(module == mod, database == database_label)
  if (nrow(df_db) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  top_terms_per_ct <- df_db %>%
    group_by(celltype) %>%
    arrange(p.adjust) %>%
    slice_head(n = n_top) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pull(Description) %>%
    unique()
  
  if (length(top_terms_per_ct) > 12) {
    top_terms_per_ct <- df_db %>%
      group_by(Description) %>%
      summarise(best_p = min(p.adjust), .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(best_p) %>%
      slice_head(n = 12) %>%
      pull(Description)
  }
  
  df_plot <- df_db %>%
    filter(Description %in% top_terms_per_ct) %>%
    mutate(neg_log_fdr = -log10(p.adjust)) %>%
    order_go_terms(desc_col = "Description", p_col = "p.adjust")
  
  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = celltype, y = Description)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_fdr), color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", neg_log_fdr)),
              size = 3.5, color = "white", fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#4575b4", high = "#d73027",
                        name = "-log10(FDR)",
                        limits = c(0, max(df_plot$neg_log_fdr, na.rm = TRUE))) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(48)) +
    labs(x = "Cell type",
         y = paste0(database_label, " term"),
         title = paste0("Module ", mod, " - ", database_label, " Terms by Cell Type (FDR < 0.05)")) +
    theme_pub(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 11),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, lineheight = 0.85),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}

# --- Reestructuración completa del ensamblado PDF con Patchwork -------------
build_module_publication_figure <- function(mod) {
  p_heatmap <- plot_module_heatmap_by_celltype(mod)
  p_counts  <- plot_module_celltype_counts(mod)
  p_trend   <- plot_module_trend_by_celltype(mod)
  
  if (is.null(p_heatmap)) p_heatmap <- patchwork::plot_spacer()
  if (is.null(p_counts))  p_counts  <- patchwork::plot_spacer()
  if (is.null(p_trend))   p_trend   <- patchwork::plot_spacer()
  
  # Fila superior (Expresión, Composición y Trayectoria)
  top <- p_heatmap + p_counts + p_trend +
    patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 0.7, 1.2))
  
  # Fila inferior: Columnas estructuradas por Base de Datos (GO_BP vs Reactome).
  # Cada columna apila verticalmente Bubble (arriba) y Lollipop (abajo).
  # GO_BP y Reactome SIEMPRE ocupan su columna, incluso si el modulo no tiene
  # terminos para esa base de datos (panel vacio en ese caso, en vez de
  # desaparecer) -- no se filtra por significancia en ningun panel: eso ya
  # queda explicito en el panel lollipop (-log10 FDR) de cada columna.
  db_columns <- lapply(databases_to_plot, function(db) {
    p_bub <- plot_module_pathway_bubble(mod, db)
    p_lol <- plot_module_pathway_lollipop(mod, db)
    
    if (is.null(p_bub)) p_bub <- empty_pathway_panel(paste0(db, " - Enriched Terms"))
    if (is.null(p_lol)) p_lol <- empty_pathway_panel(paste0(db, " - Top Significance"))
    
    p_bub / p_lol + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1))
  })
  
  bottom <- patchwork::wrap_plots(db_columns, ncol = length(db_columns))
  
  # Integración final vertical
  top / bottom +
    patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.7)) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = paste0("Module ", mod, " -- expression, composition, trajectory, and pathway enrichment, all by cell type"),
      theme = theme_pub(base_size = 12)
    )
}

# --- Main rendering and saving loop -----------------------------------------
# Figura combinada (heatmap + composicion + trayectoria + pathways) para
# TODOS los modulos, no solo los significativos. Los modulos con trayectoria
# de edad significativa (p_value < 0.05, no FDR) ademas se guardan por
# duplicado con el sufijo "_significant" en el nombre del PDF, para poder
# ubicarlos rapido sin perder el set completo.
dir.create("module_trajectory_pathway_by_celltype", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("module_pathway_heatmaps", showWarnings = FALSE)

all_modules_for_figure <- module_trajectory %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p_value) %>%
  dplyr::pull(module)

for (mod in all_modules_for_figure) {
  
  cat("\n\n## Módulo:", mod, "\n\n")
  
  tryCatch({
    p_full <- build_module_publication_figure(mod)
    
    if (!is.null(p_full)) {
      print(p_full)
    }
    
    base_path <- file.path("module_trajectory_pathway_by_celltype",
                           paste0("module_", mod, "_trajectory_pathways.pdf"))
    save_pub_pdf(p_full, filename = base_path, width = 22, height = 14)
    
    row_traj <- module_trajectory %>% dplyr::filter(module == mod)
    is_significant <- nrow(row_traj) == 1 && !is.na(row_traj$p_value) && row_traj$p_value < 0.05
    
    if (is_significant) {
      sig_path <- file.path("module_trajectory_pathway_by_celltype",
                            paste0("module_", mod, "_trajectory_pathways_significant.pdf"))
      file.copy(base_path, sig_path, overwrite = TRUE)
      cat("  -> age-associated (p =", signif(row_traj$p_value, 3),
          "), copy saved as", basename(sig_path), "\n")
    }
    
    for (db in databases_to_plot) {
      p_heatmap_db <- create_module_pathway_heatmap(mod, db, n_top = 8)
      if (!is.null(p_heatmap_db)) {
        save_pub_pdf(p_heatmap_db,
                     filename = paste0("module_pathway_heatmaps/", db, "_heatmap_module_", mod, ".pdf"),
                     width = 10,
                     height = 8)
      }
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(paste0("Error processing module ", mod, ": ", e$message))
  })
}

```

## Trajectory + GO terms per module x cell-type combination, stacked by cell type

The combined per-module figure above overlays all cell types in one
trajectory panel and pools GO terms across cell types. This section
instead builds **one row per (module, cell type) combination**: the
cell-type-restricted eigengene trajectory for that combination alone
(its own panel, not overlaid with other cell types), with the top
significant **GO Biological Process** terms *for that same cell type
only* right next to it. Rows are then stacked vertically into **one
figure per cell type** (4 figures total, one per target cell type),
ordered by how significant that module's overall age trajectory is.

Cell type color is kept consistent with the rest of the report (same
`viridis`/`"turbo"` palette used in the combined per-module figure), so
a given cell type is always the same color across every plot.

```{r module-celltype-combo-setup}
# `celltype_colors` and `order_go_terms()` were already defined earlier
# (module-trajectory-pathway-figure chunk) and are reused here so cell-type
# colors stay identical across every plot in the report.

# --- Trajectory panel: ONE cell type, its own cell-type-restricted eigengene
plot_celltype_module_trend <- function(mod, ct) {
  df <- compute_celltype_module_eigengene(mod, ct)
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  col_ct <- unname(celltype_colors[ct])
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = age, y = ME)) +
    geom_point(color = col_ct, size = 2.2, alpha = 0.75) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 1.3, se = TRUE,
                color = col_ct, fill = col_ct, alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = "Cell-type-restricted eigengene",
         title = paste0("Module ", mod, " -- ", ct),
         subtitle = paste0("n genes = ", unique(df$n_genes))) +
    theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, color = "grey40")
    )
}

# --- GO panel: top significant GO_BP terms for THIS module x cell type only
plot_celltype_module_go_terms <- function(mod, ct, n_terms = 10) {
  df <- enrichment_by_module_celltype %>%
    filter(module == mod, celltype == ct, database == "GO_BP") %>%
    # guard against duplicate term rows (e.g. re-run enrichment merges) so
    # the same GO term is never plotted twice for this module x cell type
    dplyr::distinct(Description, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    arrange(p.adjust) %>%
    slice_head(n = n_terms)
  
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = paste0("No significant GO BP terms\n(", ct, ")"),
                 size = 3.2, color = "grey40") +
        theme_void()
    )
  }
  
  col_ct <- unname(celltype_colors[ct])
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      neg_log_fdr = -log10(p.adjust),
      Description = factor(Description, levels = rev(Description))
    )
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = neg_log_fdr, y = Description)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = neg_log_fdr, y = Description, yend = Description),
                 color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(aes(size = Count), color = col_ct, alpha = 0.9) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "N genes", range = c(2, 7)) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(40)) +
    labs(x = "-log10(FDR)", y = NULL,
         title = paste0("Top GO Biological Process terms -- ", ct)) +
    theme_pub(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 7.5, lineheight = 0.85),
      plot.title       = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", color = col_ct),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position  = "right",
      legend.key.size  = unit(0.3, "cm")
    )
}

# --- One row = trajectory (left) + matching GO terms (right), for one combo
build_module_celltype_combo_row <- function(mod, ct) {
  p_trend <- plot_celltype_module_trend(mod, ct)
  if (is.null(p_trend)) return(NULL)
  p_go <- plot_celltype_module_go_terms(mod, ct)
  p_trend + p_go + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.4))
}
```

```{r module-celltype-combo-stacked-by-celltype, fig.width=12, fig.height=14}
conflicts_prefer(base::unname)
dir.create("module_celltype_trajectory_GO_stacked", showWarnings = FALSE)

for (ct in sort(target_celltypes)) {
  
  # Módulos con trayectoria de edad significativa y genes presentes en este tipo celular,
  # ordenados por p-valor de la trayectoria (más significativo primero)
  mods_this_ct <- gene_celltype_module %>%
    dplyr::filter(celltype == ct, module %in% significant_trajectory_modules) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(module) %>%
    dplyr::pull(module)
  
  mods_this_ct <- module_trajectory %>%
    dplyr::filter(module %in% mods_this_ct) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p_value) %>%
    dplyr::pull(module)
  
  if (length(mods_this_ct) == 0) {
    cat("[", ct, "] No hay módulos con trayectoria significativa y genes asignados -- omitiendo.\n", sep = "")
    next
  }
  
  # Generar lista de filas pareadas ignorando valores nulos
  row_list <- purrr::compact(
    lapply(mods_this_ct, function(mod) build_module_celltype_combo_row(mod, ct))
  )
  
  if (length(row_list) == 0) {
    cat("[", ct, "] Sin filas válidas para graficar -- omitiendo.\n", sep = "")
    next
  }
  
  col_ct <- if (exists("celltype_colors") && ct %in% names(celltype_colors)) {
    unname(celltype_colors[ct])
  } else {
    "grey20"
  }
  
  n_mods <- length(row_list)
  
  # Apilado vertical con Patchwork
  p_stack <- patchwork::wrap_plots(row_list, ncol = 1) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(ct, " — Module Trajectories & Top GO Biological Process Terms"),
      subtitle = paste0(
        n_mods, " module", ifelse(n_mods > 1, "s", ""),
        " with a significant age trajectory (p_value < 0.05) and genes from ", ct, "\n",
        "(Trajectory restricted to this cell type; GO terms restricted to this cell type)"
      ),
      theme = theme_pub(base_size = 12) +
        theme(
          plot.title    = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = col_ct),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", lineheight = 1.1)
        )
    )
  
  # Mostrar gráfica en la sesión interactiva / informe HTML
  print(p_stack)
  
  # Cálculo dinámico de altura para el PDF (base de título + 3.2 in por módulo)
  pdf_height <- max(4.5, 3.2 * n_mods + 1.2)
  file_out <- paste0("module_celltype_trajectory_GO_stacked/", ct, "_modules_trajectory_GO.pdf")
  
  save_pub_pdf(
    p_stack,
    filename = file_out,
    width = 12,
    height = pdf_height
  )
  
  cat("[", ct, "] PDF generado: ", file_out, " (", n_mods, " módulos, alto = ", round(pdf_height, 1), " in)\n", sep = "")
}
```

## Master heatmap: pathway enrichment across all modules and cell types (GO / KEGG / Reactome)

Large, publication-ready heatmap showing pathway enrichment across the
entire analysis, generated once per database via a shared function.

```{r master-pathway-heatmap, fig.width=16, fig.height=12}


build_master_pathway_heatmap <- function(database_label, n_per_module = 6, n_terms_max = 20) {
  df_all <- enrichment_by_module_celltype %>%
    filter(module %in% significant_trajectory_modules, database == database_label) %>%
    mutate(neg_log_fdr = -log10(p.adjust))

  if (nrow(df_all) == 0) return(NULL)

  top_terms_per_module <- df_all %>%
    group_by(module, Description) %>%
    summarise(best_fdr = min(p.adjust), n_ct = n_distinct(celltype), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(best_fdr) %>%
    group_by(module) %>%
    slice_head(n = n_per_module) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pull(Description) %>%
    unique()

  if (length(top_terms_per_module) > n_terms_max) {
    top_terms_per_module <- df_all %>%
      group_by(Description) %>%
      summarise(best_p = min(p.adjust), .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(best_p) %>%
      slice_head(n = n_terms_max) %>%
      pull(Description)
  }

  df_master <- df_all %>%
    filter(Description %in% top_terms_per_module) %>%
    mutate(module_celltype = paste(module, celltype, sep = " / "),
           Description = factor(Description, levels = rev(sort(top_terms_per_module))))

  ggplot(df_master, aes(x = module_celltype, y = Description)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = neg_log_fdr), color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(data = df_master %>% filter(neg_log_fdr > 0),
              aes(label = sprintf("%.0f", neg_log_fdr)),
              size = 3, color = "white", fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7fbff", high = "#08519c",
                         name = "-log10(FDR)",
                         limits = c(0, max(df_master$neg_log_fdr, na.rm = TRUE)),
                         na.value = "#f7fbff") +
    labs(x = "Module / Cell Type",
         y = paste0(database_label, " term"),
         title = paste0(database_label, " Enrichment: All Significant Modules and Cell Types")) +
    theme_pub(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 15)),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.key.height = unit(0.5, "cm"),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(r = 20)
    )
}

for (db in c("GO_BP", "KEGG", "Reactome")) {
  p_master_db <- build_master_pathway_heatmap(db)
  if (!is.null(p_master_db)) {
    print(p_master_db)
    save_pub_pdf(p_master_db,
                 filename = paste0(db, "_master_heatmap_all_modules.pdf"),
                 width = 16,
                 height = 12)
    cat("Saved master", db, "heatmap to plots_pdf/", db, "_master_heatmap_all_modules.pdf\n")
  } else {
    cat("No significant", db, "results to build a master heatmap for.\n")
  }
}
```

## Additional exploratory visualizations

Six extra views of the same underlying tables (`gene_celltype_module`,
`MEs`, `module_trajectory`, `enrichment_by_module_celltype`) -- no new
data is computed upstream of this section, only new plots.

### 1. Module membership (kME) by cell type, hub genes highlighted

For every module, kME (module membership) of every gene is plotted
against the cell type it came from (jittered), with **hub genes** (the
same top-10% kME definition used in `hub_genes_table`) highlighted in
red. This is the plot-equivalent of `hub_genes_by_module.csv`: instead
of scrolling a table, you see at a glance whether hub genes concentrate
in one cell type or are spread across all of them, and how kME is
distributed overall.

```{r kme-jitter-setup}
gene_celltype_module <- gene_celltype_module %>%
  mutate(is_hub = gene_celltype %in% hub_genes_table$gene_celltype)

plot_kme_jitter_module <- function(mod) {
  df <- gene_celltype_module %>% filter(module == mod, !is.na(kME))
  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)

  ggplot(df, aes(x = celltype, y = kME)) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = is_hub, size = is_hub, alpha = is_hub),
                width = 0.28, height = 0) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#d73027", "FALSE" = "grey65"),
                        labels = c("TRUE" = "Hub gene (top 10% kME)", "FALSE" = "Other gene"),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_size_manual(values = c("TRUE" = 2.3, "FALSE" = 1.1), guide = "none") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c("TRUE" = 0.9, "FALSE" = 0.35), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "Cell type", y = "kME (module membership)",
         title = paste0("Module ", mod, " -- module membership by cell type")) +
    theme_pub(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "top",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
    )
}
```

### 2. Alluvial / Sankey diagram: module -\> cell type composition

Flow diagram where the left axis is module, the right axis is cell type,
flow width is the number of genes -- the same information as the
composition heatmap (`heatmap_composicion_celular_por_modulo.pdf`), but
easier to scan when there are many modules: dominant cell types per
module jump out as thick flows. Flows and the module axis are colored by
the module's own WGCNA color.

```{r module-celltype-alluvial, fig.width=12, fig.height=max(6, 0.35 * length(unique(gene_counts_by_module_celltype$module)))}
alluvial_data <- gene_counts_by_module_celltype %>%
  filter(module != "grey") %>%
  mutate(module_color = tolower(module))

# Order modules by total size (top to bottom) for a cleaner read
module_order <- alluvial_data %>%
  group_by(module) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n_genes), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  pull(module)

alluvial_data <- alluvial_data %>%
  mutate(module = factor(module, levels = module_order))

p_alluvial <- ggplot(alluvial_data,
                      aes(axis1 = module, axis2 = celltype, y = n_genes)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = module_color), width = 1/6, alpha = 0.85, color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/6, fill = "grey92", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2.8) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Module", "Cell type"), expand = c(0.08, 0.08)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of genes",
       title = "Module -> cell type composition (all genes)") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  )

print(p_alluvial)
save_pub_pdf(p_alluvial, "alluvial_module_celltype_composition.pdf",
             width = 12, height = max(6, 0.35 * length(unique(alluvial_data$module))))

# Second version restricted to modules with a significant age trajectory,
# for a less crowded "what matters" view
if (length(significant_trajectory_modules) > 0) {
  alluvial_sig <- alluvial_data %>% filter(as.character(module) %in% significant_trajectory_modules)

  p_alluvial_sig <- ggplot(alluvial_sig,
                            aes(axis1 = module, axis2 = celltype, y = n_genes)) +
    geom_alluvium(aes(fill = module_color), width = 1/6, alpha = 0.85, color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    geom_stratum(width = 1/6, fill = "grey92", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 3.2) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Module", "Cell type"), expand = c(0.08, 0.08)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of genes",
         title = "Module -> cell type composition (significant age-trajectory modules only)") +
    theme_pub(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)
    )

  print(p_alluvial_sig)
  save_pub_pdf(p_alluvial_sig, "alluvial_module_celltype_composition_significant.pdf",
               width = 10, height = 7)
}
```

### 3. Jaccard overlap matrix between modules

Pairwise Jaccard index (shared genes / union of genes, gene identity
only -- cell-type origin is ignored so a gene shared across cell types
within a module counts once) between every pair of modules, as a
symmetric heatmap. High off-diagonal values flag potentially redundant
modules (near-duplicate gene sets) that might be candidates for merging
in a future run; low values everywhere confirm the modules are capturing
distinct biology.

```{r module-jaccard-overlap, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
gene_sets_by_module <- gene_celltype_module %>%
  filter(module != "grey") %>%
  distinct(module, gene) %>%
  split(x = .$gene, f = .$module)

mods_jaccard <- names(gene_sets_by_module)

jaccard_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(mods_jaccard), ncol = length(mods_jaccard),
                       dimnames = list(mods_jaccard, mods_jaccard))

for (i in seq_along(mods_jaccard)) {
  for (j in i:length(mods_jaccard)) {
    a <- gene_sets_by_module[[mods_jaccard[i]]]
    b <- gene_sets_by_module[[mods_jaccard[j]]]
    j_val <- length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
    jaccard_mat[i, j] <- j_val
    jaccard_mat[j, i] <- j_val
  }
}

# Order modules by hierarchical clustering on (1 - Jaccard) distance, so
# similar modules sit next to each other in the heatmap
jaccard_dist  <- as.dist(1 - jaccard_mat)
jaccard_hclust <- hclust(jaccard_dist, method = "average")
mod_order_jaccard <- mods_jaccard[jaccard_hclust$order]

jaccard_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(jaccard_mat)) %>%
  setNames(c("module_1", "module_2", "jaccard")) %>%
  mutate(
    module_1 = factor(module_1, levels = mod_order_jaccard),
    module_2 = factor(module_2, levels = mod_order_jaccard)
  )

p_jaccard <- ggplot(jaccard_df, aes(x = module_1, y = module_2, fill = jaccard)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#08519c", limits = c(0, 1),
                       name = "Jaccard\nindex") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Pairwise gene-set overlap between modules (Jaccard index)",
       subtitle = "Off-diagonal values close to 1 flag potentially redundant modules") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey35")
  ) +
  coord_fixed()

print(p_jaccard)
save_pub_pdf(p_jaccard, "module_jaccard_overlap_heatmap.pdf", width = 9, height = 8)

# Flag any pair (excluding self) above a redundancy threshold, for a quick text summary
redundancy_threshold <- 0.3
redundant_pairs <- jaccard_df %>%
  filter(as.character(module_1) < as.character(module_2), jaccard >= redundancy_threshold) %>%
  arrange(desc(jaccard))

cat("Module pairs with Jaccard >=", redundancy_threshold, "(possible redundancy):\n")
if (nrow(redundant_pairs) > 0) print(redundant_pairs) else cat("None.\n")
```

### 4. PCA of module eigengenes (MEs) by mouse, colored by age

Instead of looking at trajectories one module at a time, this projects
**all mice into the joint module-eigengene space** (PCA on `MEs`, grey
module excluded) and colors each mouse by its real age. If aging has a
coherent, dataset-wide signature across modules (not just isolated
single-module trends), mice should separate along a smooth age gradient
in this space.

```{r me-pca-by-age, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
MEs_no_grey <- MEs[, !grepl("^MEgrey$", colnames(MEs)), drop = FALSE]

pca_me <- prcomp(MEs_no_grey, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
pca_var <- round(100 * (pca_me$sdev^2) / sum(pca_me$sdev^2), 1)

pca_df <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rownames(MEs_no_grey),
  PC1 = pca_me$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_me$x[, 2],
  age = age_num_lookup[rownames(MEs_no_grey)]
)

p_pca_me <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = age)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = sample_id), size = 2.5, color = "grey30",
                            max.overlaps = 15, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Age", option = "plasma") +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", pca_var[1], "% variance)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", pca_var[2], "% variance)"),
       title = "PCA of module eigengenes (MEs) across mice",
       subtitle = "Grey (unassigned) module excluded; color = real age") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey35"))

print(p_pca_me)
save_pub_pdf(p_pca_me, "PCA_module_eigengenes_by_age.pdf", width = 9, height = 7)

# UMAP version, only if the 'uwot' package is available (optional dependency
# -- PCA above already gives the core result, UMAP is a bonus nonlinear view)
if (requireNamespace("uwot", quietly = TRUE) && nrow(MEs_no_grey) > 15) {
  set.seed(1)
  umap_me <- uwot::umap(scale(MEs_no_grey), n_neighbors = min(10, nrow(MEs_no_grey) - 1))
  umap_df <- data.frame(
    sample_id = rownames(MEs_no_grey),
    UMAP1 = umap_me[, 1],
    UMAP2 = umap_me[, 2],
    age = age_num_lookup[rownames(MEs_no_grey)]
  )

  p_umap_me <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = age)) +
    geom_point(size = 3.2, alpha = 0.9) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = sample_id), size = 2.5, color = "grey30",
                              max.overlaps = 15, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Age", option = "plasma") +
    labs(title = "UMAP of module eigengenes (MEs) across mice",
         subtitle = "Grey (unassigned) module excluded; color = real age") +
    theme_pub(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey35"))

  print(p_umap_me)
  save_pub_pdf(p_umap_me, "UMAP_module_eigengenes_by_age.pdf", width = 9, height = 7)
} else {
  cat("'uwot' not installed (or too few mice) -- skipping the UMAP version; PCA above already computed.\n")
}
```

### 5. All module trajectories, combined in a single figure (small multiples)

One combined figure with **every module** (not only the significant
ones), one facet each, ordered by trajectory p-value -- a fast visual
scan of shapes (Increasing / Decreasing / U-shaped / Inverted U-shaped)
without opening every individual PDF. Point/line color = the module's
own WGCNA color, for consistency with the other figures in this report.
Modules associated with age are defined here as **p-value \< 0.05**
(raw, not FDR-adjusted) and are flagged with a "\*" in the facet label,
so the combined figure and the age-association call use the same, single
criterion.

```{r all-trajectories-facet, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
all_trajectory_modules <- module_trajectory %>% dplyr::arrange(p_value) %>% dplyr::pull(module)

if (length(all_trajectory_modules) > 0) {
  traj_long <- df_traj %>%
    dplyr::select(sample_id, age_num,
                  all_of(paste0("ME", all_trajectory_modules))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(sample_id, age_num), names_to = "module", values_to = "ME") %>%
    mutate(module = sub("^ME", "", module)) %>%
    left_join(module_trajectory %>% dplyr::select(module, category, shape, p_value),
              by = "module") %>%
    mutate(
      module = factor(module, levels = all_trajectory_modules),
      module_color = tolower(as.character(module)),
      is_age_associated = p_value < 0.05,
      module_label = paste0(as.character(module), ifelse(is_age_associated, " *", ""),
                             " -- ", category,
                             " (p = ", signif(p_value, 2), ")")
    )

  # keep facet order = p-value order (most significant first)
  label_order <- traj_long %>% distinct(module, module_label) %>% arrange(module) %>% pull(module_label)
  traj_long <- traj_long %>% mutate(module_label = factor(module_label, levels = label_order))

  p_traj_facet <- ggplot(traj_long, aes(x = age_num, y = ME)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = module_color), size = 1.8, alpha = 0.65) +
    geom_smooth(aes(color = module_color, fill = module_color),
                method = "loess", span = 1.3, se = TRUE, alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    facet_wrap(~module_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = "Module eigengene",
         title = "All module trajectories, combined",
         subtitle = "\"*\" in facet title = module associated with age (p-value < 0.05, not FDR)") +
    theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30")
    )

  print(p_traj_facet)
  n_facets <- length(unique(traj_long$module))
  save_pub_pdf(p_traj_facet, "all_module_trajectories_combined.pdf",
               width = 14, height = max(6, 3 * ceiling(n_facets / 4)))
} else {
  cat("No modules with a computed trajectory -- skipping the facet comparison.\n")
}
```

Modules associated with age (p-value \< 0.05, not FDR):

```{r age-associated-modules-summary}
age_associated_modules_table <- module_trajectory %>%
  dplyr::filter(p_value < 0.05) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p_value) %>%
  dplyr::select(module, shape, category, p_value, fdr, r_squared)

cat("Modules associated with age (p_value < 0.05):\n")
print(age_associated_modules_table)
```

### 6. Gene-concept network (cnetplot) for the top modules

For the modules with the strongest age trajectories, a gene-concept
network connects each module's top enriched GO Biological Process terms
to the genes that support them (pooled across cell types, unlike the
by-cell-type enrichment used elsewhere). Node color = kME (module
membership) of that gene, so hub genes stand out visually inside the
network. Recomputed fresh here (readable `enrichResult` objects aren't
kept from the by-cell-type enrichment above, since `cnetplot()` needs
the actual `enrichResult`, not the flattened data frame) -- limited to a
handful of top modules to keep this fast.

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)

if (requireNamespace("conflicted", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(conflicted)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select,   .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter,   .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::mutate,   .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::arrange,  .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::count,    .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::rename,   .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::slice,    .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(dplyr::first,    .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(base::intersect, .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(base::union,     .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(base::setdiff,   .quiet = TRUE)
  conflicts_prefer(stats::cor,      .quiet = TRUE)
}

n_top_modules_cnet <- min(6, length(significant_trajectory_modules))
top_modules_cnet <- head(significant_trajectory_modules, n_top_modules_cnet)

dir.create("cnetplot_top_modules_by_celltype", showWarnings = FALSE)

module_celltype_combos <- gene_celltype_module %>%
  dplyr::filter(module %in% top_modules_cnet) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(module, celltype)

cnet_results_summary <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(module_celltype_combos))) {
  mod <- module_celltype_combos$module[i]
  ct  <- module_celltype_combos$celltype[i]
  combo_label <- paste(mod, ct, sep = "_")
  
  tryCatch({
    genes_mod_ct <- gene_celltype_module %>%
      dplyr::filter(module == mod, celltype == ct) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(gene) %>%
      dplyr::pull(gene)
    
    if (length(genes_mod_ct) < 5) {
      message("Module ", mod, " / ", ct, ": <5 genes -- skipping.")
      next
    }
    
    entrez_mod_ct <- convert_to_entrez_flexible(
      setNames(list(genes_mod_ct), combo_label), min_genes = 5, verbose = FALSE
    )
    if (length(entrez_mod_ct) == 0 || is.null(entrez_mod_ct[[combo_label]])) {
      message("Module ", mod, " / ", ct, ": too few genes mapped to Entrez -- skipping cnetplot.")
      next
    }
    
    ego_mod_ct <- clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
      gene          = entrez_mod_ct[[combo_label]],
      universe      = universe_entrez,
      OrgDb         = org.Mm.eg.db,
      ont           = "BP",
      pAdjustMethod = "BH",
      pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
      qvalueCutoff  = 0.2,
      readable      = TRUE
    )
    
    if (is.null(ego_mod_ct) || nrow(as.data.frame(ego_mod_ct)) == 0) {
      message("Module ", mod, " / ", ct, ": no significant GO_BP terms -- skipping cnetplot.")
      next
    }
    
    # 1. Asegurar vector fc_vec sin duplicados ni NAs
    fc_df <- gene_kme_lookup %>%
      dplyr::filter(module == mod) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)
    
    fc_vec <- fc_df$kme
    names(fc_vec) <- fc_df$gene
    fc_vec <- na.omit(fc_vec)
    
    # 2. Generar cnetplot (se retira scale_color_gradient2 directo para evitar conflictos de ggraph)
    p_cnet <- enrichplot::cnetplot(
      ego_mod_ct, 
      foldChange = fc_vec, 
      showCategory = min(6, nrow(as.data.frame(ego_mod_ct))),
      node_label = "all", 
      cex_label_gene = 0.6, 
      cex_label_category = 0.8
    ) +
      labs(title = paste0("Module ", mod, " | ", ct, " -- gene-concept network (GO_BP)")) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
    
    # Renderizar en consola/pantalla
    print(p_cnet)
    
    # 3. Guardar con ggsave (o sustituir por save_pub_pdf si está definida en tu entorno)
    ggplot2::ggsave(
      filename = paste0("cnetplot_top_modules_by_celltype/module_", combo_label, "_cnetplot.pdf"),
      plot = p_cnet,
      width = 11, 
      height = 9
    )
    
    # 4. Registrar solo si la gráfica y el guardado se completaron sin errores
    cnet_results_summary[[combo_label]] <- nrow(as.data.frame(ego_mod_ct))
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Module ", mod, " / ", ct, ": cnetplot failed -> ", conditionMessage(e))
  })
}

cat("\nCombinaciones módulo x celltype procesadas con éxito:\n")
if (length(cnet_results_summary) > 0) {
  print(cnet_results_summary)
} else {
  cat("Ninguna combinación generó un gráfico con éxito.\n")
}
```
